name: The keeper's quarters at the Chicago light
aka: the quarters of the Chicago lighthouse keepership

documented_range.note: NEITHER END IS DATED BY A SOURCE. THE START is the light itself: Samuel Jackson completed the second tower in 1832, and the keepership Andreas records — Samuel Lasby, the first keeper, 'at $350 a year with quarters' — is an office that exists from the night the light was first kept. A station's quarters are not later than its light. THE END is the scene's own window and not a statement about the building: nothing reached says when these quarters were replaced, and the 1835-12-31 bound is the honest limit of what this project's corpus covers rather than a fate. Both ends are inferred for those reasons.

position.symbolic_location: On the Fort Dearborn Reservation at the mouth of the river, about twenty-four metres west of the 1832 light tower on the same flat at the inside of the bend, on the landward side of the tower and clear of the garrison's barn.
position.note: PLACED AGAINST THE TOWER AND NOT AGAINST THE GROUND, and the direction and the distance are invented. No source of any kind puts these quarters anywhere: 'with quarters' is a term of the appointment and not a description of a site. METHOD: the coordinate is an offset of 23.7 m due west of this project's own committed position for chicago_lighthouse_1832 — itself read off Wright's 1834 sheet in 2026-09-12 (T-1065) and carrying about 22 m of its own uncertainty. WEST was taken for two reasons that are reasoning rather than reading: it keeps the house on the landward side of the tower, away from the water at the inside of the bend, and it is the only quadrant that clears both the garrison's big barn (fort_dearborn_big_barn, 32 m away on this line; 14 m if the house were set south-west) and the fort's own ground east of the light. The working uncertainty is therefore the tower's 22 m plus the whole of the unstated offset — call it 40 m, the same figure the agency log houses' notes carry for the same kind of placement. The ground here is the e1834_harbor_cut heightfield at +2.45 m above the summer-1835 water surface, 0.03 m below the tower's own sample, so the house stands on traced ground and declares no ground contact. Facade bearing 90 — the door east, toward the light it served — is invented; nothing states it.

derivation.reason: The evidence is one phrase about a salary. There is no reading to re-derive a coordinate from, and the offset from the tower is this project's own choice.

footprint.note: PLACEHOLDER — NO DIMENSION IS ATTESTED. 6.1 x 4.9 m is about 20 x 16 ft, a one-room-and-a-half dwelling of the size a single federal appointment at $350 a year was housed in. Every number is invented; the sources give a salary, a reflector and a height of tower, and no dimension of any dwelling.

construction.note: INVENTED, AND THE ONE ATTRIBUTE HERE THAT A SOURCE COULD EASILY HAVE SETTLED. Nothing states what the quarters were built of. Frame is taken because the works at this station were federal contract carpentry under Samuel Jackson and because a dwelling raised beside a masonry tower in 1832 on the Michigan shore is as likely to be sawn frame as it is to be logs — which is an argument about the decade and the paymaster, not about this house. Log would be the equally defensible reading, and that is what makes this reconstructed rather than inferred — the generator builds it at 1.0 confidence, which is the massing the eye should read as ours. L287 owns it.

stories.note: Not attested. A single keeper's dwelling at a frontier light station is a one-storey house; the reading this project already gives the small dwellings of this scene.

wall_height_m.note: No figure is attested. 2.4 m is about 8 ft, the archetype's low band and the figure the other small dwellings of this scene carry.

roof_type.note: Not attested. Gable is the near-universal roof form for a small dwelling of this type, period and region.

roof_pitch_deg.note: No pitch is attested. 38 degrees is the archetype's mid-range for a small frame dwelling. Inferred from practice, not measured.

chimneys.note: Not attested. Quarters kept through a Chicago winter by a man who watched a light all night cooked and heated at a hearth, so the record carries one stack; where it stood is not stated and the archetype places it against the gable end.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this record wears 4.5 in — dealt by tools/deal_siding_stock.py: keyed to the phase's construction season, because buildings sided from the same season's shipments of St Joseph sawn lumber tend toward one stock, then advanced so no frame building within 60 m shares this one's. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention.

phases.change_note: Raised 2026-09-28 (T-1716). New record; nothing moved. The tower's own record is untouched.

function.note: THE QUARTERS ARE THE DOCUMENTED PART OF THE APPOINTMENT. Andreas gives the first keeper of this light $350 a year AND QUARTERS; a keepership paid partly in housing is evidence that housing stood at the station, and a light kept nightly was kept by somebody who slept beside it. What the phrase does NOT give is a building: it does not say a separate house, it does not say where, and it does not say what of. So the USE is inferred from the terms of a federal appointment, and every drawn attribute of the thing that carries the use is invented under L287. Read at docs/RESEARCH/chicago_lighthouse_1832.md § 4 and data/reconstruction/1835_institutional_lodging.json.

research_note: RAISED BECAUSE A HOUSEHOLD WAS SLEEPING IN A FORTY-FOOT MASONRY TOWER. `data/reconstruction/1835_institutional_lodging.json` admitted one household to the town's nine institutional roofs — the keeper's, at `chicago_lighthouse_1832` — on the grounds that the keepership was paid 'with quarters' and 'no keeper's dwelling is modelled, so the quarters this project can account for are at the light itself'. That row also recorded what it cost: its own card refuses to draw a household size, because 'drawing 4.4 people into a forty-foot tower would be the model reaching past the one thing the record gives it'. The defect was never the adjudication; it was that the project had no roof for it to point at. This record is that roof, and the bed moves to it. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: who kept the light on 1835-07-01 (Andreas has Lasby first, Wentworth has William M. Stevens only from October 1836, and no source reached covers the gap), how many people the quarters held, what they were built of, how large they were, or where at the station they stood. No occupant is written on this record: the household is the reconstruction's own, it lives on its card, and a source naming the keeper retires the invention rather than joining it. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE THIS RECORD: the Light-House Board's annual reports or the Fifth Auditor's returns, which paid the keeper and would describe his quarters; a keeper's return; or a measured reading of the 1850 von Schneidau daguerreotype or the 1855 Hesler photograph, in both of which the station stands. See docs/RESEARCH/chicago_lighthouse_1832.md § 4 and docs/LIBERTIES.md L287.

land_owner.value: The ground was entered by John Baptist Baubian, 28 May 1835
land_owner.note: THE UNITED STATES RESERVATION. This is the same tract L108 already derives for `1835_no_build_ground.json` — from G1, Madison's line and the traced waterline — so the polygon is inherited rather than built again, and `check.sh` already re-derives it. The register's own row is the second, independent witness to the date L108 quotes from Andreas: Beaubien's pre-emption, 28 May 1835, five weeks before the scene date. The derived polygon is short of the documented 75.69 acres for the reasons L108 states, and is a floor rather than the reservation. WHETHER THE ENTRY HELD IS NOT READ HERE: it was disputed, and this row records the entry the register carries and nothing about its outcome. THE MARGIN IS ONLY 21 m, which is inside the working horizontal uncertainty of the georeference (about 20 m) doubled, so the grade drops a tier: the tract is right if the constructed line is, and nothing here proves the line to better than that. WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It claims that the tract the Illinois State Archives' land-sale register describes contains this structure's committed position — the patent for this ground was ENTERED by this man on this date. It does not claim he still held the ground on 1 July 1835, that he lived here, or that he ever stood on it: a sale is a transaction, and the register's only column about residence names a county. THE SECTION LINES ARE CONSTRUCTED, NOT TRACED (L219): the grid is carried from the single PLSS corner at State & Madison, on the plat's own east-west bearing, in nominal one-mile squares.
land_owner.tract: the south-west fractional quarter of section 10
